questions.stem: A nurse earns an annual salary of $78 000. Taking 1 year as 52 weeks, what is the weekly pay?
questions.explanation: Weekly pay = 78 000 ÷ 52 = $1500. $6500 is the monthly pay (÷ 12) and $3000 is the fortnightly pay (÷ 26).

questions.stem: An engineer's annual salary is $91 260. What is the fortnightly pay?
questions.explanation: There are 26 fortnights in 52 weeks, so 91 260 ÷ 26 = $3510. $3802.50 divides by 24, which treats a year as 12 months of exactly two fortnights each.

questions.stem: A worker is paid $5200 per month. Taking 1 year as 52 weeks, what is the equivalent weekly pay?
questions.explanation: Annual pay = 5200 × 12 = $62 400, and 62 400 ÷ 52 = $1200. $1300 divides the monthly pay by 4, but a month is longer than 4 weeks.

questions.stem: Job A pays $1450 per week. Job B pays $6200 per month. Which pays more per year, and by how much?
questions.explanation: Job A: 1450 × 52 = $75 400. Job B: 6200 × 12 = $74 400. Job A pays $1000 more. Treating a month as 4 weeks makes Job B look better, which is why both must be converted to a year.

questions.stem: A shop assistant earns $28.40 per hour and works 38 hours in a week. What is the weekly wage?
questions.explanation: Wage = 28.40 × 38 = $1079.20. Each of the other amounts corresponds to a different number of hours: 37.5, 39 and 36.

questions.stem: A mechanic earns $32 per hour for a 38-hour week. One week she also works 4 hours of overtime at time-and-a-half. What is her pay for the week?
questions.explanation: Normal pay: 38 × 32 = $1216. Overtime: 4 × 32 × 1.5 = $192. Total $1408. $1344 pays the overtime hours at the normal rate.

questions.stem: A café worker's normal rate is $27.50 per hour. On Sundays he is paid double time. How much does he earn for a 6-hour Sunday shift?
questions.explanation: Double time is 2 × 27.50 = $55 per hour, and 6 × 55 = $330. $247.50 uses time-and-a-half instead of double time.

questions.stem: A worker's normal rate is $30 per hour. One week she works 35 normal hours, 3 hours at time-and-a-half and 2 hours at double time. What is her total pay?
questions.explanation: 35 × 30 = $1050, 3 × 30 × 1.5 = $135 and 2 × 30 × 2 = $120, giving $1305. $1200 pays all 40 hours at the normal rate.

questions.stem: A nurse earns $26 per hour and works 8 hours on a public holiday at double time and a half. What is the pay for that shift?
questions.explanation: Double time and a half is 2.5 × the normal rate: 8 × 26 × 2.5 = $520. $416 is double time and $312 is time-and-a-half.

questions.stem: A worker earned $1197 for 36 normal hours plus 4 hours of overtime at time-and-a-half. What is the normal hourly rate?
questions.explanation: The 4 overtime hours are worth 4 × 1.5 = 6 normal hours, so the pay equals 36 + 6 = 42 normal hours: 1197 ÷ 42 = $28.50. $29.93 divides by 40, ignoring the overtime loading.

questions.stem: A car salesperson earns 4% commission on sales. What is the commission on $85 000 of sales?
A salesperson receives a retainer of $450 per week plus 5% commission on sales. What is the total pay in a week with $12 400 of sales?
questions.explanation: Commission = 0.05 × 12 400 = $620, and the total pay is 450 + 620 = $1070. $620 leaves out the retainer, and $642.50 takes 5% of the retainer as well as the sales.

questions.stem: Commission is paid at 5% on the first $50 000 of sales, 3% on the next $100 000 and 2% on sales above $150 000. What is the commission on sales of $210 000?
questions.explanation: 5% of 50 000 = $2500, 3% of 100 000 = $3000, and 2% of the remaining 60 000 = $1200, a total of $6700. $10 500 applies 5% to all the sales, and $4200 applies 2% to all of them.

questions.stem: A real estate agent earns 2.5% commission on the first $500 000 of a sale price and 1.5% on the remainder. What is the commission on a house that sells for $820 000?
questions.explanation: 0.025 × 500 000 = $12 500 and 0.015 × 320 000 = $4800, a total of $17 300. $20 500 applies 2.5% to the whole price, and $12 300 applies 1.5% to the whole price.

questions.stem: A factory worker is paid $0.85 for each item completed. How much does she earn for 1240 items?
questions.explanation: Piecework pay = 0.85 × 1240 = $1054. $1458.82 divides 1240 by 0.85 instead of multiplying.

questions.stem: A fruit picker is paid $2.40 per bag. How many bags must he fill to earn $600?
questions.explanation: Bags = 600 ÷ 2.40 = 250. 1440 multiplies 600 by 2.40 instead of dividing.

questions.stem: An author receives a royalty of 10% of the selling price of each book. The book sells for $32.95 and 4000 copies are sold. What is the royalty?
questions.explanation: Total sales = 32.95 × 4000 = $131 800, and 10% of that is $13 180. $131 800 is the total sales, before the royalty rate is applied.

questions.stem: A songwriter's royalty is 8% of sales on the first 5000 copies and 12% on every copy after that. Each copy sells for $25 and 9000 copies are sold. What is the royalty?
A government allowance pays $412.50 per fortnight. Taking 1 year as 52 weeks, how much is this per year?
questions.explanation: There are 26 fortnights in a year, so 412.50 × 26 = $10 725. $21 450 multiplies by 52, treating the fortnightly amount as weekly.

questions.stem: A sole trader electrician receives $96 000 from customers in a year and has $21 500 of business expenses. What are the electrician's earnings from the business?
questions.explanation: A sole trader's earnings are the business income minus business expenses: 96 000 − 21 500 = $74 500. $96 000 counts all the money received, ignoring the costs of running the business.

questions.stem: A worker's normal pay is $1200 per week. She takes 4 weeks of annual leave with a leave loading of 17.5%. What is the leave loading?
questions.explanation: Leave loading = 17.5% of the normal pay for the leave: 0.175 × 4 × 1200 = 0.175 × 4800 = $840. $210 is the loading for one week only.

questions.stem: A worker earns $1340 per week and takes 4 weeks of annual leave with a 17.5% leave loading. What is the total holiday pay?
questions.explanation: Normal pay for 4 weeks = $5360, and the loading = 0.175 × 5360 = $938, so the total is $6298. $5360 leaves out the loading, and $938 is the loading alone.

questions.stem: An employee earns $31 per hour for a 38-hour week. She takes 4 weeks of annual leave, with a leave loading of 17.5% of normal pay. What is her total pay for the leave?
questions.explanation: Normal pay = 31 × 38 × 4 = $4712. Loading = 0.175 × 4712 = $824.60. Total = $5536.60. $4712 is the pay before the loading is added.

questions.stem: A spreadsheet has an employee's weekly base wage in B2 and weekly sales in C2. Commission is 4% of sales. Which formula gives the total weekly pay?
questions.explanation: The base wage is paid in full and 4% of sales is added: B2 + 0.04 × C2. =(B2+C2)*0.04 takes 4% of the base wage too, and =B2+4*C2 uses 4 instead of 0.04.

questions.stem: A worker's gross income for the year is $72 400 and her allowable deductions are $2650. What is her taxable income?
questions.explanation: Taxable income = gross income − allowable deductions = 72 400 − 2650 = $69 750. $75 050 adds the deductions instead of subtracting them.

questions.stem: Which of these is usually an allowable tax deduction for an employee?
options: Protective clothing needed to do the job
Travel between home and the workplace
questions.explanation: Deductions are expenses incurred in earning the income, such as protective clothing needed for work. Ordinary travel from home to work and everyday clothes are private expenses, even though they are linked to going to work.

questions.stem: Use this tax scale: $0 to $18 200, nil; $18 201 to $37 000, 19c for each $1 over $18 200; $37 001 to $87 000, $3572 plus 32.5c for each $1 over $37 000. What is the tax payable on a taxable income of $52 000?
questions.explanation: 52 000 is in the third bracket: 3572 + 0.325 × (52 000 − 37 000) = 3572 + 4875 = $8447. $4875 leaves out the $3572 for the lower brackets, and $16 900 applies 32.5c to every dollar.

questions.stem: Use this tax scale: $0 to $18 200, nil; $18 201 to $37 000, 19c for each $1 over $18 200; $37 001 to $87 000, $3572 plus 32.5c for each $1 over $37 000. What is the tax payable on a taxable income of $30 000?
questions.explanation: 30 000 is in the second bracket: 0.19 × (30 000 − 18 200) = 0.19 × 11 800 = $2242. $5700 applies 19c to the whole income, including the tax-free $18 200.

questions.stem: Use this tax scale: $0 to $18 200, nil; $18 201 to $37 000, 19c for each $1 over $18 200; $37 001 to $87 000, $3572 plus 32.5c for each $1 over $37 000. A worker's gross income is $68 500 and her allowable deductions are $1500. What tax is payable?
questions.explanation: Taxable income = 68 500 − 1500 = $67 000. Tax = 3572 + 0.325 × (67 000 − 37 000) = 3572 + 9750 = $13 322. $13 809.50 uses the gross income without taking off the deductions.

questions.stem: Use this tax scale: $0 to $18 200, nil; $18 201 to $37 000, 19c for each $1 over $18 200; $37 001 to $87 000, $3572 plus 32.5c for each $1 over $37 000. A worker's taxable income rises from $40 000 to $41 000. How much extra tax is payable?
questions.explanation: Both incomes are in the third bracket, so each extra dollar is taxed at 32.5c: 0.325 × 1000 = $325. $190 uses the 19c rate, which applies only up to $37 000.

questions.stem: In a spreadsheet, a taxable income between $18 201 and $37 000 is in cell A2. The tax is 19c for each $1 over $18 200. Which formula calculates the tax?
questions.explanation: Only the amount over $18 200 is taxed, at 0.19 per dollar, so the subtraction must be inside the brackets. =0.19*A2-18200 subtracts after multiplying, and 19 is in cents rather than dollars.

questions.stem: Under the Pay-As-You-Go (PAYG) system, how is an employee's income tax collected during the year?
options: The ATO deducts tax from the employee's bank account each month
The employee pays tax only on overtime and bonuses during the year
The employer withholds tax from each pay and sends it to the ATO
The employee pays all the year's tax in one sum after the tax return
questions.explanation: Under PAYG the employer withholds an amount from each pay, using tax tables, and passes it to the Australian Taxation Office. At the end of the year the tax return compares this with the tax actually payable.

questions.stem: Taking the Medicare levy as 2% of taxable income, what is the levy on a taxable income of $65 000?
A worker has a gross income of $84 000 and allowable deductions of $3500. Taking the Medicare levy as 2% of taxable income, what is the levy?
questions.explanation: Taxable income = 84 000 − 3500 = $80 500, and 2% of that is $1610. $1680 takes 2% of the gross income, before deductions.

questions.stem: A worker's weekly gross pay is $1450. Each week $298 tax is withheld, $46 is deducted for health insurance and $9 for union fees. What is the net pay?
questions.explanation: Net pay = 1450 − 298 − 46 − 9 = $1097. $1152 subtracts only the tax, and $1106 leaves out the union fees.

questions.stem: After a tax return, a worker's tax payable plus Medicare levy is $16 400. Her employer withheld $17 020 under PAYG. What is the result?
questions.explanation: More was withheld than is payable, so the difference, 17 020 − 16 400 = $620, is refunded. She would owe money only if the amount withheld were less than the tax payable.

questions.stem: Use this tax scale: $0 to $18 200, nil; $18 201 to $37 000, 19c for each $1 over $18 200; $37 001 to $87 000, $3572 plus 32.5c for each $1 over $37 000. A worker earns $2400 per fortnight for 26 fortnights, and $462 PAYG tax is withheld from each pay. Her allowable deductions are $1400, and the Medicare levy is 2% of taxable income. What is the result of her tax return?
questions.explanation: Gross income $62 400, so taxable income is $61 000. Tax = 3572 + 0.325 × 24 000 = $11 372, Medicare = $1220, total $12 592. Withheld = 462 × 26 = $12 012, so she owes $580. A refund of $640 forgets the Medicare levy.
